sections.heading: Stoichiometry, Concentration Terms & Redox Titrations
sections.summary: Mole equals mass / molar mass = N / N_A = V(L at STP 22.7 L / NTP 22.4 L). Normality = Molarity x n-factor.
keyPoints: Temperature-independent concentrations: Molality (m = mol solute / kg solvent), Mole fraction (X), % w/w. Temperature-dependent: Molarity (M), Normality (N).
Law of Equivalence: mEq of Oxidant = mEq of Reductant => N1 V1 = N2 V2.
Key n-factors: KMnO4 = 5 (acidic -> Mn^2+), 3 (neutral -> MnO2), 1 (alkaline -> MnO4^2-); K2Cr2O7 = 6 (acidic -> 2 Cr^3+); H2C2O4 = 2.

sections.heading: Bohr Atom & Quantum Mechanical Orbitals (Psi^2)
sections.summary: Wavefunction Psi(r, theta, phi) yields probability density |Psi|^2; nodes are regions of zero electron probability.
keyPoints: Bohr velocity v = 2.18 x 10^6 (Z/n) m/s; Radius r_n = 0.529 (n^2 / Z) A; Energy E_n = -13.6 (Z^2 / n^2) eV.
Quantum number constraints: n >= 1; l in [0 .. n-1]; m_l in [-l .. +l]; s = +/- 1/2.
Radial (spherical) nodes = n - l - 1; Angular (planar/conical) nodes = l; Total nodes = n - 1.

formulas.note: d = solution density in g/mL
Rules out fixed trajectories for microscopic electrons

formulas.formula: Radial = n - l - 1 ; Angular = l ; Total = n - 1
formulas.note: 4p orbital has 2 radial nodes and 1 angular node

traps: Molarity changes when temperature rises because solution volume expands; Molality & Mole fraction never change with T!
Number of spectral lines emitted from level n2 down to ground n1=1 is n2(n2 - 1)/2, NOT just n2 - 1!

solvedExamples.question: How many moles of KMnO4 in acidic medium are needed to oxidize 1 mole of Ferrous Oxalate (FeC2O4) completely?
steps: Fe^2+ -> Fe^3+ (1e-) AND C2O4^2- -> 2 CO2 (2e-) => total n-factor of FeC2O4 = 1 + 2 = 3.
n-factor of KMnO4 (acidic) = 5.
n_KMnO4 x 5 = 1 x 3 => n_KMnO4 = 3/5 = 0.6 mole.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Forgetting that BOTH Fe^2+ and oxalate C2O4^2- get oxidized gives wrong answer 0.2 or 0.4!

sections.heading: Periodic Trends & Ionization / Electron Gain Exceptions
sections.summary: Half-filled and completely-filled subshells create crucial bumps across Period 2/3 ionization and electron affinity trends.
keyPoints: IE1 Period 2: Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne (Be > B because 2s^2; N > O because 2p^3 half-filled!).
Electron Gain Enthalpy (magnitude): Cl > F > Br > I (2p compact inter-electronic repulsion makes F slightly less exothermic than Cl!); similarly S > O.
Isoelectronic cations shrink with higher nuclear charge: Al^3+ < Mg^2+ < Na^+ < F^- < O^2- < N^3-.

sections.heading: VSEPR Shapes, Hybridization, MOT & Fajan's Rules
sections.summary: Steric number = sigma bonds + lone pairs determines electron geometry; lone-pair positions determine final molecular shape.
keyPoints: Key anomalous shapes: SF4 (See-Saw sp3d), ClF3 (T-shaped sp3d), XeF2 (Linear sp3d), XeF4 (Square Planar sp3d2), IF7 (Pentagonal Bipyramidal).
MOT s-p mixing (<= 14 e- like B2, C2, N2): pi_2px = pi_2py sits LOWER than sigma_2pz! Hence B2 (10e-) is paramagnetic while C2 (12e-, BO=2) is diamagnetic.
For >14 e- (O2, F2): sigma_2pz is lower; O2 has 2 unpaired pi* electrons (paramagnetic, BO=2). Superoxide O2^- BO=1.5; O2^+ BO=2.5.

formulas.note: V = central valence e-, M = monovalent H/X atoms, C = cation charge, A = anion charge
Higher BO -> stronger bond -> shorter bond length

formulas.formula: Small Cation + Large Anion + High Charge
formulas.note: Pseudo-noble d^10 (Cu+/Ag+) polarizes far stronger than s^2p^6

traps: NO2, ClO2, CO2 vs SO2: CO2 has 0 dipole moment (linear), whereas BF3, XeF4, PCl5, SF6 also have EXACT zero dipole moment due to symmetry cancellation!
H-bond strength order: HF > H2O > NH3 per bond, YET H2O has HIGHER boiling point than HF because H2O forms 4 H-bonds per molecule in 3D network!

solvedExamples.question: Arrange O2^+, O2, O2^-, O2^2- in increasing order of O-O bond length.
steps: Bond length varies inversely with Bond Order: O2^+ < O2 < O2^- < O2^2-.
solvedExamples.pitfall: O2, O2^+, O2^- are all paramagnetic; ONLY peroxide O2^2- is diamagnetic!

sections.heading: Chemical Thermodynamics: Enthalpy, Hess Law & Spontaneity
sections.summary: Enthalpy change Delta H = Delta U + Delta n_g R T bridges bomb calorimeter measurements (q_v = Delta U) to constant pressure heat (q_p = Delta H).
keyPoints: Standard Enthalpy of Formation Delta H_f = 0 ONLY for reference elemental states (O2(g), C(graphite), S8(rhombic), Br2(l)); diamond != 0!
Bond enthalpy shortcut: Delta H_rxn = Sum BE(reactants) - Sum BE(products) [NOTE: Reactants MINUS Products!].
Gibbs Free Energy: Delta G = Delta H - T Delta S. Process is spontaneous when Delta G < 0. If Delta H < 0 and Delta S > 0 -> spontaneous at ALL T!

sections.heading: Liquid Solutions: Raoult's Law & Van't Hoff Factor (i)
sections.summary: Colligative properties depend purely on total solute particle concentration: multiply m or M by Van't Hoff factor i = 1 + (n - 1)alpha.
keyPoints: Positive Raoult deviation (A-B weaker than A-A/B-B): Ethanol + Water -> Minimum boiling azeotrope (Delta H_mix > 0, Delta V_mix > 0).
Negative Raoult deviation (A-B H-bonding stronger): CHCl3 + Acetone, HNO3 + Water -> Maximum boiling azeotrope.
Osmotic pressure pi = i C R T is the BEST method for macromolecules (proteins/polymers) since measurements work cleanly at room T.

formulas.formula: Delta G deg = -2.303 R T log10(K_eq)
formulas.note: Delta G = 0 at equilibrium, NOT Delta G deg!

formulas.formula: dT_b = i K_b m ; dT_f = i K_f m
formulas.note: Cryoscopic K_f(H2O) = 1.86, K_b(H2O) = 0.52 K.kg/mol

formulas.formula: (P0 - P) / P0 = i n_solute / (i n_solute + n_solvent)
formulas.note: Exact Raoult form vs dilute approximation

comparison.title: Signs of Delta H & Delta S for Spontaneity

traps: Chemistry Physics Sign Flip: Chemistry dU = q + w with w = -P_ext dV! Never mix Physics +P dV with Chemistry -P dV!
0.1 M BaCl2 (i=3) has HIGHER boiling point and LOWER freezing point than 0.1 M NaCl (i=2) or 0.1 M Urea (i=1)!

solvedExamples.question: Calculate the freezing point of an aqueous solution containing 0.1 mol/kg K4[Fe(CN)6] assuming 80% dissociation (K_f = 1.86 K.kg/mol).
steps: K4[Fe(CN)6] -> 4 K^+ + [Fe(CN)6]^4- gives n = 5 ions.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Always subtract dT_f from 0 deg C (273.15 K) for freezing point depression!

sections.heading: Chemical Equilibrium & Le Chatelier's Principle
sections.summary: Equilibrium constant K depends STRICTLY on temperature (van't Hoff equation); catalysts & inert gas at constant volume do NOT shift equilibrium.
keyPoints: Kp = Kc (R T)^(Delta n_g), where Delta n_g counts strictly GASEOUS products minus reactants.
Reversing reaction inverts K -> 1/K; multiplying by coefficient m raises K -> K^m; adding two steps multiplies K1 * K2.
Raising pressure shifts toward FEWER gas moles; raising T favors ENDOTHERMIC (Delta H > 0) direction.

sections.heading: Ionic Equilibrium: Buffers, Salt Hydrolysis & Ksp
sections.summary: Ostwald dilution works for weak electrolytes; common ion suppresses both weak acid ionization and sparingly soluble salt solubility.
keyPoints: Henderson Buffer: Acidic pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]); Basic pOH = pKb + log([Salt]/[Base]). Max capacity at [Salt] = [Acid].
Salt of Weak Acid + Weak Base (CH3COONH4): pH = 7 + (pKa - pKb)/2 (INDEPENDENT of concentration!).
Solubility Product: AB -> S^2; A2B/AB2 -> 4 S^3; A3B/AB3 -> 27 S^4. Precipitation happens ONLY when Qsp > Ksp.

formulas.note: Independent of dilution concentration
Occurs when conjugate ratio = 1

formulas.formula: K_h = K_w / K_a ; pH = 7 + (pKa + log C)/2
formulas.note: Solution is basic (pH > 7)

traps: 10^(-8) M HCl has pH = 6.96 (NEVER 8!), because auto-ionization of water [H+] = 10^(-7) M must be included!
Adding inert gas at CONSTANT VOLUME changes zero partial pressures -> ZERO shift; at CONSTANT PRESSURE it acts like volume expansion!

solvedExamples.question: Calculate pH of buffer obtained by mixing 100 mL of 0.2 M CH3COOH (pKa = 4.76) with 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH.
steps: Initial mmoles: CH3COOH = 20, NaOH = 10.
After neutralization: remaining CH3COOH = 10 mmol, formed CH3COONa = 10 mmol.
solvedExamples.pitfall: At half-neutralization point of any weak acid titration, pH equals pKa directly!

sections.heading: Electrochemistry: Nernst, Faraday & Conductance
sections.summary: EMF E_cell = E_cathode - E_anode (SRP); cell works spontaneously when E_cell > 0 and Delta G = -n F E_cell < 0.
keyPoints: Nernst Equation at 298 K: E_cell = E deg_cell - (0.0591 / n) log10(Q). At equilibrium, E_cell = 0 => E deg_cell = (0.0591 / n) log10(K_c).
Faraday's Law: Deposited mass w = (E_eq * Q) / 96500 = (M * I * t) / (n * 96500).
Kohlrausch Law: Lambda_m deg = sum of ionic conductivities. On dilution, specific conductivity kappa DECREASES while molar conductivity Lambda_m INCREASES!

sections.heading: Chemical Kinetics: Order, Molecularity & Arrhenius
sections.summary: Order is experimental sum of concentration exponents in Rate = k[A]^x[B]^y; molecularity applies strictly to elementary single steps.
keyPoints: Zero order: [A] = [A]_0 - k t; t_1/2 = [A]_0 / (2k); units mol L^(-1) s^(-1). Rate never drops until reactant finishes.
Arrhenius: k = A e^(-Ea / RT) => log(k2 / k1) = (Ea / 2.303 R) (1/T1 - 1/T2). Catalyst lowers Ea WITHOUT shifting Delta H, Delta G or K_eq!

formulas.formula: E3 deg = (n1 E1 deg + n2 E2 deg) / n3
formulas.note: E deg is INTENSIVE (add Delta G deg = -nFE deg, NEVER add E deg directly!)
For A(g) -> B(g) + C(g) decomposition

comparison.title: Zero vs First vs Second Order Kinetics

traps: NEVER add or subtract electrode potentials directly when finding a third half-cell E deg; ALWAYS convert to Delta G deg = -n F E deg!
For electrolysis of aqueous NaCl vs dilute H2SO4, check overpotential: Cl2 evolves over O2 at anode when concentrated!

solvedExamples.question: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 40 minutes. How long does 99.9% completion take?
steps: 75% complete = 2 half-lives (25% left) => 2 t_1/2 = 40 min => t_1/2 = 20 min.
99.9% complete = 10 half-lives (0.1% ~= 1/1024 left) => t_99.9% = 10 x 20 = 200 minutes.

sections.heading: p-Block General Anomalies & d-f Block Metallurgy Trends
sections.summary: Inert pair effect stabilizes LOWER oxidation states down heavy p-block groups (Tl^+, Pb^2+, Bi^3+ > Tl^3+, Pb^4+, Bi^5+).
keyPoints: Boiling point Group 15 hydrides: BiH3 > SbH3 > NH3 > AsH3 > PH3; Group 16: H2O >> H2Te > H2Se > H2S.
Lanthanoid Contraction (poor 4f shielding) makes Zr & Hf (and Nb & Ta) nearly identical atomic radii.
KMnO4 oxidizes I^- to I2 (acidic) and IO3^- (neutral/faintly alkaline)! K2Cr2O7 flips orange Cr2O7^2- (acid) <-> yellow CrO4^2- (base).

sections.heading: Coordination Compounds: Isomerism, VBT & Crystal Field Theory
sections.summary: Ligand field strength splits degenerate d-orbitals into t2g (lower) and eg (higher) in octahedral complexes.
keyPoints: Spectrochemical Series: CO, CN^- > en > NH3 > NCS^- > H2O > OH^- > F^- > Cl^- > Br^- > I^-.
High-spin vs Low-spin (d^4 - d^7): Strong field causes pairing; Co^3+ behaves strong-field even with H2O & C2O4^2-!
Tetrahedral splitting Delta_t = (4/9) Delta_o (< Pairing energy P) => almost ALWAYS high spin! Spin-only magnetic moment mu = sqrt(n(n+2)) BM.

formulas.formula: CFSE = (-0.4 n_t2g + 0.6 n_eg) Delta_o + m P
formulas.note: d^3, d^8, d^9 have identical e- arrangement in both weak & strong fields
n = unpaired d electrons; n=4 -> sqrt(24) ~= 4.90 BM
All 3 are classic Coordination VBT exam favorites!

traps: AgCl/HgCl2/PbCl2/Cu2Cl2 covalent chlorides do NOT respond positively to Chromyl Chloride orange-red CrO2Cl2 fumes!
In metal carbonyls M-CO, M->C pi back-bonding STRENGTHENS M-C bond while WEAKENING C-O triple bond order!

solvedExamples.question: How many stereoisomers (geometrical + optical) exist for [Co(en)2 Cl2]^+?
steps: Geometrical forms: cis-[Co(en)2 Cl2]^+ and trans-[Co(en)2 Cl2]^+.
trans isomer has horizontal symmetry plane => optically INACTIVE (1 isomer).
cis isomer lacks plane/centre of symmetry => exists as d, l enantiomeric pair (2 isomers).
Total stereoisomers = 1 + 2 = 3.
solvedExamples.pitfall: [Ma2b2c2] octahedral has 5 geometrical (6 stereoisomers total) — memorize common counts!

sections.heading: Electronic Effects, Aromaticity & Acid-Base Strength
sections.summary: Carbocations & free radicals stabilize via +I, +M, and hyperconjugation (alpha-H count); carbanions stabilize via -M and -I.
keyPoints: Acidic order: RSO3H > RCOOH > H2CO3 > Phenol > H2O > ROH > HC#CH > NH3 > RCH=CH2 > RH.
Ortho effect makes o-substituted benzoic acids STRONGER than benzoic acid; SIR weakens aniline basicity (o-methylaniline weakest!).
Huckel Rule: Cyclic, planar, conjugated with (4n + 2) pi electrons = Aromatic (C5H5^-, C7H7^+, Benzene); 4n pi = Anti-aromatic (C4H4, unstable!).

sections.heading: Isomerism & Hydrocarbon Reactions
sections.summary: Chiral molecules lack plane (POS) and centre (COS) of symmetry. Reductive ozonolysis cleaves C=C into C=O aldehydes/ketones.
keyPoints: CIP Priority (R/S, E/Z): higher atomic number = higher priority. If lowest group #4 sits on horizontal wedge, flip R <-> S!
Hydroboration-Oxidation (BH3 / H2O2, OH^-): syn-addition, anti-Markovnikov alcohol without carbocation rearrangement.
Benzene EAS: -OH, -NH2, -OR, -R are ortho/para activating; -NO2, -CN, -CHO, -COOH are meta deactivating; Halogens (-Cl/-Br) are ortho/para YET deactivating (-I > +M).

formulas.note: Each ring or pi bond adds +1 to DBE; triple bond = +2
cis-alkene + anti = racemic (d+l); trans-alkene + anti = meso!
Differentiates 1-alkyne from 2-alkyne cleanly

traps: Kharasch Peroxide Effect works EXCLUSIVELY with HBr — NEVER with HCl or HI (thermodynamically unfavorable propagation steps)!
2-3-Dichlorobutane has two identical chiral centres -> 1 meso + 1 d,l pair = 3 stereoisomers (NOT 2^2 = 4!).

solvedExamples.question: Which symmetrical alkene produces exclusively acetone (CH3COCH3) on reductive ozonolysis (O3 / Zn-H2O)?
steps: Join two carbonyl carbons of CH3-C(=O)-CH3 back with a C=C double bond removing both oxygens.
Yields (CH3)2C=C(CH3)2 -> 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Oxidative ozonolysis (O3 / H2O2) turns aldehydes further into -COOH acids while keeping ketones unchanged!

sections.heading: Haloalkanes (SN1/SN2/E1/E2) & Phenols / Ethers
sections.summary: Substrate steric hindrance vs carbocation stability decides SN2 (1 deg, inversion, polar aprotic) vs SN1 (3 deg/allylic, racemic, polar protic).
keyPoints: E2 elimination requires ANTI-PERIPLANAR H and leaving group, yielding Zaitsev more-substituted alkene (unless bulky t-BuOK -> Hofmann!).
Lucas Test (conc. HCl + anhy. ZnCl2): 3 deg alcohol gives immediate turbidity; 2 deg in 5 min; 1 deg no reaction at room T.
Phenol + CHCl3 + KOH -> Salicylaldehyde (Reimer-Tiemann); Phenol + CO2 + NaOH -> Salicylic acid (Kolbe). Anisole + HI -> Phenol + CH3I (NEVER iodobenzene!).

sections.heading: Carbonyls, Carboxylic Acids & Amines
sections.summary: Nucleophilic addition reactivity drops as Aldehyde > Ketone because of steric & +I crowding; Amines basicity balances +I, solvation & sterics.
keyPoints: Aldol Condensation requires alpha-H (dil. NaOH -> alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl); Cannizzaro requires ZERO alpha-H (HCHO, PhCHO, Me3CCHO -> alcohol + carboxylate).
Tollens / Fehling reduce ONLY aldehydes (NOTE: Benzaldehyde reduces Tollens ONLY, NOT Fehling!). Haloform (I2/NaOH) tests CH3CO- and CH3CH(OH)- groups.
Aqueous amine basicity: Methylamines 2 deg > 1 deg > 3 deg > NH3; Ethylamines 2 deg > 3 deg > 1 deg > NH3. Gabriel Phthalimide makes pure 1 deg aliphatic amines (NEVER Ar-NH2!).

formulas.note: Requires alpha-H on carboxylic acid
Removes ONE carbonyl carbon cleanly; 100% retention of chiral centre
Cu2Cl2, KI, HBF4(Balz-Schiemann Ar-F), CuCN

rows: 1 deg (soluble in KOH), 2 deg (insoluble), 3 deg (no rxn)

traps: Methanol (CH3OH) does NOT give Iodoform; Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) IS the ONLY primary alcohol giving positive yellow CHI3!
Aniline does NOT undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation because Lewis acid AlCl3 binds strongly to basic -NH2 forming salt!

solvedExamples.question: Identify final product: Benzamide + Br2/aq.KOH -> (A) -> + NaNO2/HCl (0-5 deg C) -> (B) -> + H3PO2/H2O -> (C).
steps: Hoffmann Bromamide turns Benzamide (Ph-CONH2) into Aniline Ph-NH2 (A).
Diazotization at 0-5 deg C produces Benzene diazonium chloride Ph-N2^+ Cl^- (B).
Hypophosphorous acid H3PO2 reduces diazonium salt smoothly to Benzene (C).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Using EtOH instead of H3PO2 also reduces PhN2+ to Benzene (producing CH3CHO).

sections.heading: Biomolecules: Carbohydrates, Amino Acids & Nucleic Acids
sections.summary: Carbohydrates vary between reducing (hemiacetal/hemiketal free) and non-reducing (Sucrose locked C1-C2 glycosidic bond).
keyPoints: Sucrose (C1 alpha-Glc + C2 beta-Fru) is non-reducing, shows NO mutarotation, and converts (+66.5 deg -> -39.9 deg) levo on inversion!
Maltose = alpha-D-Glc(1->4) (reducing); Lactose = beta-D-Gal(1->4)beta-D-Glc (reducing). Cellulose = beta-D-Glc; Starch = alpha-D-Glc.
Zwitterion amino acid Isoelectric point pI = (pKa1 + pKa2) / 2. RNA contains Uracil; DNA has Thymine (2-deoxyribose).

sections.heading: Principles Related to Practical Chemistry (Qualitative Salt Analysis)
sections.summary: Group separation relies on selective precipitation using Common Ion Suppression of H2S / NH4OH.
keyPoints: Group I (dil. HCl): Pb^2+, Ag^+, Hg2^2+. Group II (HCl + H2S, low [S^2-]): Cu^2+, Pb^2+, Hg^2+, Cd^2+, Bi^3+, As^3+.
Group III (NH4Cl + NH4OH): Al^3+ (white gelatinous), Fe^3+ (reddish brown), Cr^3+ (green). Group IV (NH4OH + H2S): Zn^2+ (white), Mn^2+ (buff), Co^2+/Ni^2+ (black).
Anion tests: Nitrate Brown Ring [Fe(H2O)5 NO]^2+; Lassaigne Nitrogen Prussian Blue Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3; Sulphur Purple [Fe(CN)5 NOS]^4-.

formulas.note: Thiourea (N+S together) gives blood-red [Fe(SCN)]^2+ unless excess Na splits it!
Iron oxidation state in brown complex is +1!

formulas.formula: B1: Beri-Beri | C: Scurvy | B12: Pernicious Anaemia
formulas.note: Fat-soluble A, D, E, K stored in liver; B & C water-soluble

traps: NH4Cl is added BEFORE NH4OH in Group III to suppress OH^- concentration via common ion NH4^+ so Mg(OH)2 / Group IV do NOT precipitate prematurely!
Invert sugar: Sucrose itself is dextrorotatory (+66.5 deg), yet equimolar mixture of Glucose (+52.5 deg) & Fructose (-92.4 deg) turns net optical rotation levorotatory!

solvedExamples.question: Why does an acidic solution of Fructose still reduce Fehling's and Tollens' reagents even though it is a ketohexose?
steps: In alkaline Tollens' / Fehling's medium, Fructose undergoes Lobry de Bruyn-van Ekenstein enediol tautomerization.
It isomerizes reversibly into D-Glucose and D-Mannose (aldehydes), giving bright positive silver mirror / brick-red Cu2O!
solvedExamples.answer: Enediol tautomerization in basic medium yields aldoses
solvedExamples.pitfall: Ketones normally fail Tollens' — alpha-hydroxy ketones (fructose, benzoin) are crucial exceptions!

sections.heading: Real Gases: Van der Waals & Compressibility Z
sections.summary: Deviations from PV = nRT arise from intermolecular attraction (a) and finite molecular co-volume (b = 4 x actual volume).
keyPoints: (P + a n^2 / V^2)(V - n b) = n R T. At low P: Z = 1 - a/(VRT) < 1; at high P: Z = 1 + Pb/(RT) > 1.
Hydrogen & Helium show Z > 1 at ALL pressures at room T due to tiny 'a'!
Critical constants: V_c = 3b, P_c = a/(27b^2), T_c = 8a/(27Rb), Universal Z_c = P_c V_c / (R T_c) = 3/8 = 0.375. Boyle Temp T_B = a/(Rb).

sections.heading: Solid State: Bravais Lattices, Voids & Ionic Crystals
sections.summary: Density rho = (Z * M) / (N_A * a^3). Void placement determines ionic stoichiometry and radius ratios.
keyPoints: Cubic Packing: SC (Z=1, 52.4%, 2r=a); BCC (Z=2, 68%, 4r=sqrt(3)a); FCC/CCP (Z=4, 74%, 4r=sqrt(2)a, CN=12).
In CCP/FCC with N atoms: Octahedral voids = N (12 edge centres + 1 body centre); Tetrahedral voids = 2N (2 along each of 4 body diagonals at r = sqrt(3)a/4).
Defects: Schottky (equal cation-anion missing -> density DROPS, NaCl/CsCl); Frenkel (cation slips to interstitial -> density UNCHANGED, AgCl/ZnS).

formulas.note: Boyle Temp T_B is 3.375 times critical temperature T_c
Keep a in cm for g/cm^3 (1 pm = 10^(-10) cm)
CsCl = Cubic (8:8); NaCl = Octahedral (6:6); ZnS = Tetrahedral (4:4)

traps: AgBr exhibits BOTH Schottky AND Frenkel defects simultaneously — an all-time IIT favorite!
Distance between two adjacent tetrahedral voids in FCC along a cell edge equals a / 2 (NOT sqrt(3)a / 2!).

solvedExamples.question: In a hypothetical ionic crystal A_x B_y, anions B form an FCC lattice while cations A occupy HALF of the tetrahedral voids. Find empirical formula.
steps: FCC anions B per unit cell = 4.
Total tetrahedral voids = 2 x 4 = 8 => occupied by A = 8 / 2 = 4.
Ratio A : B = 4 : 4 = 1 : 1 => AB (Zinc Blende / ZnS type).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Heating NaCl in Na vapour creates F-centres (anionic vacancies trapped by unpaired electrons, giving yellow colour & paramagnetism!).

sections.heading: Surface Chemistry: Freundlich Isotherm & Colloids
sections.summary: Adsorption Delta H < 0, Delta S < 0 is spontaneous at low T where T Delta S is small; Physisorption (multilayer, low dH) differs sharply from Chemisorption (monolayer, high activation E_a).
keyPoints: Freundlich Isotherm: x/m = k P^(1/n) (0 < 1/n <= 1); log(x/m) = log k + (1/n) log P.
Peptization turns fresh precipitate into stable colloid using a small amount of electrolyte sharing a common ion (e.g., Fe(OH)3 + FeCl3 -> positive sol).
Hardy-Schulze Rule: Coagulation power proportional to (valency of oppositely charged ion)^4. Positive sols (Fe2O3.xH2O, haemoglobin) vs Negative sols (As2S3, starch, gold, blood!).

sections.heading: Concentration Cells & Cell Thermodynamics
sections.summary: Concentration cells have identical electrodes with different electrolyte activities (E deg_cell = 0 identically!).
keyPoints: Cation cell Cu | Cu^2+(C1) || Cu^2+(C2) | Cu: spontaneous when C2 (cathode) > C1 (anode); E = (0.0591 / 2) log(C2 / C1).
Gibbs-Helmholtz Cell Entropy: Delta S = n F (dE / dT)_P; Delta H = -n F [E - T(dE/dT)_P].
Gold Number measures protective power of lyophilic colloids against NaCl coagulation (LOWER Gold Number = HIGHER protection: Gelatin 0.005 best!).

formulas.note: At very high pressure 1/n -> 0 (saturation); low P 1/n -> 1
Positive temperature coefficient (dE/dT > 0) means endothermic cell rxn when dH > 0

traps: Remember As2S3 sol is NEGATIVE (coagulated best by Al^3+ > Ba^2+ > Na^+), whereas Fe(OH)3 / Al(OH)3 metal hydroxide sols are POSITIVE (coagulated best by [Fe(CN)6]^4- > PO4^3- > SO4^2- > Cl^-)!
Lower Gold Number implies STRONGER protective colloid!

solvedExamples.question: Calculate EMF at 298 K of cell Pt(H2, 1 atm) | HCl (pH = 4) || HCl (pH = 2) | Pt(H2, 1 atm).
solvedExamples.pitfall: Ensure [H+] at cathode > [H+] at anode for positive EMF!

sections.heading: Hydrogen, s-Block, Boranes & Silicates
sections.summary: Electron-deficient boron hydrides and tetrahedral SiO4^4- silicate linkages exhibit hallmark 3c-2e banana and bridging oxygen patterns.
keyPoints: B2H6 (Diborane): 4 terminal 2c-2e B-H bonds + 2 bridging 3c-2e B-H-B banana bonds. With NH3 at high T forms Borazine (B3N3H6, inorganic benzene).
Orthoboric acid H3BO3 is a WEAK MONOBASIC Lewis acid (accepts OH^- from H2O -> [B(OH)4]^- + H^+).
Silicate corner sharing: Ortho (0 shared, SiO4^4-), Pyro (1 shared, Si2O7^6-), Chain (2 shared, SiO3^2-), Sheet (3 shared, Si2O5^2-), Quartz 3D (4 shared, SiO2).
H2O2 Volume strength: M = Volume Strength / 11.2; N = Volume Strength / 5.6.

sections.heading: Metallurgy & Ellingham Diagrams
sections.summary: Reduction Delta G deg = Delta H deg - T Delta S deg proceeds whenever a lower line on the Ellingham plot reduces oxides lying above it.
keyPoints: Ellingham C -> CO has NEGATIVE slope (Delta S > 0 because 2C + O2 -> 2CO increases gas moles) — slices down across metal oxide lines at high T!
Below 983 K, CO is better reducing agent for Fe2O3; above 983 K, Coke C reduces FeO directly.
Special extractions: Al via Hall-Heroult (Al2O3 + Cryolite Na3AlF6 to lower MP); Ag/Au via MacArthur cyanide leaching [Au(CN)2]^-, [Ag(CN)2]^- + Zn dust; Ni via Mond Ni(CO)4; Ti/Zr via van Arkel I2.

formulas.formula: O-Si ratio from shared corners s
formulas.note: s=0 -> SiO4^4-; s=1 -> Si2O7^6-; s=4 -> neutral SiO2
Fails for K2CO3 because KHCO3 is too soluble!

comparison.title: Metal Extraction & Refining Quick Map
rows: Froth Flotation + Bessemer Auto-reduction -> Blister Cu

traps: Cryolite (Na3AlF6) + Fluorspar (CaF2) lower melting point (~1140 K) AND boost electrical conductivity of molten alumina!
Lithium & Magnesium share striking diagonal similarity (both form normal oxides Li2O/MgO and thermal-unstable carbonates decomposing to oxides + CO2)!

solvedExamples.question: In diborane (B2H6), count the maximum number of atoms lying simultaneously in a single plane and total 3c-2e bonds.
steps: Two Boron atoms and four terminal Hydrogen atoms (6 atoms total) lie coplanar in the xy plane.
Two bridging Hydrogen atoms sit above and below this plane forming two 3c-2e banana bonds.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Diborane has ZERO B-B direct covalent bond; all 4 B-H terminal bonds are normal 2c-2e!

sections.heading: Synthetic, Elastomer & Biodegradable Polymers
sections.summary: Addition polymers retain every monomer atom (PVC, Teflon, Buna-S, Neoprene); condensation polymers eliminate H2O/NH3/HCl forming amide/ester linkages.
keyPoints: Nylon-6,6 (Hexamethylenediamine + Adipic acid); Nylon-6 (Caprolactam ring-opening).
Terylene / Dacron (Ethylene glycol + Terephthalic acid); Glyptal (Ethylene glycol + Phthalic acid).
Bakelite = Phenol + Formaldehyde (Novolac linear -> Bakelite cross-linked thermoset). Melamine + HCHO = unbreakable crockery.
Biodegradable polymers: PHBV (3-hydroxybutanoic acid + 3-hydroxypentanoic acid) and Nylon-2-nylon-6 (Glycine + Aminocaproic acid).

sections.heading: Multi-Step Organic Roadmaps & Quantitative Estimation
sections.summary: Combine functional transformations cleanly while tracking stereochemical inversion, rearrangements & elemental percentage formulas.
keyPoints: Kjeldahl Nitrogen % = (1.4 x N_acid x V_acid(mL)) / w(g). FAILS for nitro (-NO2), azo (-N=N-), and ring nitrogen (pyridine)!
Dumas Nitrogen % = (28 x V_N2(STP mL) / 22400) x (100 / w) (works universally for ALL organic nitrogen compounds!).
Carius Halogen % = (At.Wt(X) / Mol.Wt(AgX)) x (mass_AgX / w) x 100.

formulas.note: Check milliequivalents of H2SO4 consumed carefully (N = 2 x M)!
Creates disulphide S-S bridges improving elasticity
Synthetic wool fibre

traps: Natural rubber is STRICTLY cis-1,4-polyisoprene; Gutta-percha is trans-1,4-polyisoprene!
Pyridine, Azobenzene & Nitrobenzene CANNOT be estimated by Kjeldahl method because N doesn't convert to (NH4)2SO4!

solvedExamples.question: NH3 evolved from 0.7 g of an amide neutralizes 20 mL of 0.5 M H2SO4 completely. Find mass % of Nitrogen.
steps: Normality of 0.5 M H2SO4 = 2 x 0.5 = 1.0 N => mEq = 1.0 x 20 = 20.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Always convert H2SO4 Molarity to Normality (x 2) before plugging into 1.4*N*V/w!
